content: The family Erinaceidae is the sole extant family within the order Erinaceomorpha. This family includes the well-known hedgehogs, classified under the subfamily Erinaceinae, which are native to Eurasia and Africa, as well as the gymnures or moonrats, classified under the subfamily Galericinae, which are found in Southeast Asia. Historically, this family was grouped under the order Insectivora, but that order is now considered polyphyletic and obsolete. Characteristics Members of the Erinaceidae family generally exhibit a body form similar to shrews, characterized by elongated snouts and short tails. The largest species, the Greater Moonrat, can weigh up to 4 kilograms. Most species possess five toes on each foot, often equipped with strong claws adapted for digging. They also have relatively large eyes and ears. Hedgehogs are distinct in having modified hair that forms sharp spines, which serve as a protective covering over their upper body and flanks. In contrast, gymnures lack spines and are covered with normal hair. All species in this family possess anal scent glands, but these glands are particularly well-developed in gymnures, which can emit a strong odor. Erinaceids are omnivorous, with their diet primarily consisting of insects, earthworms, and other small invertebrates. They also consume seeds, fruits, and occasionally bird eggs, as well as any carrion they encounter. Their teeth are sharp and adapted for piercing invertebrate prey. The dental formula for Erinaceids is specific to their dietary needs. Hedgehogs are predominantly nocturnal, while gymnures are less strictly nocturnal and may exhibit diurnal activity. Many species construct simple burrows, while others build temporary nests on the ground using leaves and grass or take shelter in hollow logs or similar hiding places. Erinaceids are solitary animals outside of the breeding season, and males do not participate in raising the offspring. Female Erinaceids have a gestation period of approximately six to seven weeks. The young are born blind and hairless, although hedgehogs begin to develop their characteristic spines within 36 hours of birth. Evolution The Erinaceidae family represents a relatively primitive group of placental mammals, having undergone minimal evolutionary change since their origin in the Eocene epoch. One notable extinct member of this group is Deinogalerix, often referred to as the giant hedgehog (though it was actually a gymnure). This species, which lived during the Miocene in what is now Italy, was approximately the size of a large rabbit and may have fed on vertebrate prey or carrion rather than insects. Classification The family Erinaceidae comprises 10 genera and 24 species.
